# Clinic Health Dashboard Overview
A simple dashboard for Weeks 1–8 should focus on **trend visibility**, **operational pressure**, and **attendance quality**. The best fit is a 3-metric layout with one chart per metric, plus a small KPI strip at the top.

# Metric-by-Metric Chart Recommendations
Week labels: **W1–W8**

| Metric | Values | Best Chart | Why it fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patient counts | 42, 45, 47, 50, 49, 53, 58, 60 | **Line chart** | Shows steady growth and the small dip in Week 5 clearly |
| Average wait time (min) | 18, 17, 19, 20, 16, 15, 14, 13 | **Line chart** | Best for spotting the peak in Week 4 and the improvement afterward |
| No-show rate (%) | 12, 11, 10, 11, 9, 8, 7, 7 | **Line chart** | Makes the downward trend and stabilization at 7% easy to read |

## Recommended Dashboard Layout
- **Top row KPIs**
  - Total patients in Week 8: **60**
  - Latest average wait time: **13 min**
  - Latest no-show rate: **7%**
- **Main row charts**
  - Left: **Patient Count Trend**
  - Middle: **Wait Time Trend**
  - Right: **No-Show Rate Trend**
- **Bottom row**
  - Small insight panel with flags for growth, congestion, and attendance

### Why this design works
- Line charts are ideal because all three metrics are **weekly time series**
- The dashboard stays simple and manager-friendly
- It highlights operational changes without clutter

# Manager Insights to Notice
- **Patient volume is rising steadily** from 42 to 60, which suggests growing demand or improved access.
- **Wait times improved sharply after Week 4**, dropping from a peak of 20 minutes to 13 minutes by Week 8.
- **No-show rates declined from 12% to 7%**, which likely helped clinic efficiency and may be contributing to shorter waits.
